title: Tool-agnostic requirements-to-architecture contract
objective: Create the agreed shared architecture documents, reusable templates and traceable example, integrate agent entrypoints and publish a reviewed PR without merge.
approved_sources: User authorization 2026-10-20: create the discussed documents and a PR; keep complete and tool agnostic.

acceptance.description: Binding, proportionate requirements-to-architecture workflow includes ownership, source authority, iteration, traceability and distinct review/implementation/verification gates.
Reusable architecture, ADR, quality scenario, traceability, review and tool mapping templates cover the agreed information and project-specific tailoring.
A clearly hypothetical end-to-end example demonstrates derivation, many-to-many links, planned verification, unresolved decisions and change impact without invented approvals or PASS.
Official source provenance distinguishes public normative scope from Backbone rules and optional methods; no certification claim or mandatory tool/stack.
Agent/root/planning/quality/adoption entrypoints and direct-copy/legacy distribution resolve to consistent canonical guidance without overwriting project architecture.
Relevant deterministic, negative/compatibility and trusted-base checks pass; independent behavior and authority reviews are triaged and confirmed findings repaired with Delta.
Published PR binds accessible reviewed commits and patch evidence; actual publication checks and available CI results are recorded; no merge/release.

manual_evidence: Independent frozen behavior and authority Full reviews after checks; separate triage and bounded Delta as needed
Hosted CI observations on actual published head

stop_conditions: Scope or trust-boundary expansion requires updated independently reviewed plan.
Stop if source requirements or authorities conflict, required evidence cannot be obtained, or review budget is exhausted.
At most two Full rounds for this scope; triage before repair.
forbidden_actions: No merge, release, deployment, protection changes or automatic downstream apply.
No new product requirements, invented approval/test evidence, weaker local rules or tool-specific architecture mandate.
Do not include unrelated local PR18 publication repairs or change historical evidence.
